dct_description_sm: A three-day workshop was held in Charlottetown to engage First Nation communities from the Atlantic Provinces in discussions on the current knowledge and technical capacity, as well as on the risks, vulnerabilities, and priorities of Atlantic First Nation communities in terms of impacts of climate change. This project aimed to: (1) introduce participants to climate change adaptations; (2) review potential impacts on Atlantic Aboriginal communities infrastructure and other possible implications; (3) develop adaptation response agendas for the Atlantic Aboriginal Community; (4) discuss ways communities can adapt; (5) identify funding sources; and (6) emphasize keeping Aboriginal lands and treaty and gathering rights at the forefront of developing adaptation strategies.
